title: Demonstrate an understanding of the cultivation of soil and the control of weed

lessons.title: Cultivating soil in the vineyard
lessons.html:
Cultivating soil in the vineyard

Cultivation means working the soil with tools or implements. In an established vineyard or orchard, we cultivate to control weeds, to let water soak in, and to work in cover crops or compost. Too much cultivation damages the soil, so modern farms cultivate only when needed.

Ways to manage the soil between rows

  • Clean cultivation: the soil is kept bare by discs or tines. This removes weeds but leaves soil open to erosion and loses organic matter.
  • Cover crops: crops such as oats, rye, or legumes like vetch and clover are sown in autumn between rows. They protect the soil in winter, add organic matter and, for legumes, add nitrogen. In spring they are cut or rolled and left as mulch, or worked in.
  • Mulch: straw, chopped prunings or compost is spread under the vines. Mulch keeps the soil cool and moist and smothers weeds.
  • Permanent grass: short grass kept mowed between rows in some blocks.

Rules for cultivating

  • Do not cultivate deep near the vines; roots near the surface can be cut.
  • Do not work very wet soil; it causes compaction and hard clods.
  • Do not work very dry, dusty soil more than needed; it breaks down soil structure and blows away.
  • On slopes, keep cover crops or mulch to stop erosion. The Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 requires farmers to protect their soil.

Implements

Tractor implements include disc harrows, tine cultivators, mowers, rollers and weeders that work in the vine row. Only trained and authorised drivers may use them. Workers on foot stay well clear of working implements and never ride on them.

lessons.title: Controlling weeds in the vineyard
lessons.html:
Controlling weeds in the vineyard

Weeds compete with vines for water and nutrients, especially in spring and early summer and in young vineyards. They can also hide pests, raise the humidity around bunches and make work difficult. The area directly under the vines (the vine row) is the most important to keep clean.

Methods of weed control

MethodExamples
PreventiveClean implements so weed seeds are not carried from block to block; stop weeds from making seed
MechanicalHoeing by hand, tine weeders, mowing, discing between rows
CulturalCover crops and mulch that smother weeds
ChemicalHerbicides applied by trained operators

Hand hoeing around vines

  • Hoe shallowly, just under the surface.
  • Keep the hoe away from the trunk. Bark wounds let in diseases and can kill young vines.
  • Remove the whole root of perennial weeds like kweek and uintjies.
  • Do not cover drip lines with soil, and do not cut them.

Herbicides

Herbicides are registered agricultural remedies under Act 36 of 1947 and must be used as the label says. In a vineyard:

  • only trained, authorised workers may spray them, wearing the PPE on the label;
  • keep spray off the green leaves and shoots of the vines, and off young vine stems; many herbicides damage vines;
  • never spray in wind, because spray drifts onto vines;
  • follow the label for rates and any waiting periods;
  • clean equipment and store chemicals in the locked store.

Common vineyard weeds

Kweek (couch grass), uintjies (nutgrass), ryegrass, bindweed and khakibos. Your supervisor will show you the ones on your farm.

Key points

  • Cultivate only when needed and never deep near the vines.
  • Do not work very wet soil; protect slopes with cover crops or mulch.
  • Cover crops and mulch protect soil and smother weeds.
  • Keep the vine row clean of weeds, without damaging trunks or drip lines.
  • Only trained workers apply herbicides, as the label says, keeping spray off the vines.

quiz.question: What is a benefit of a legume cover crop such as vetch?

options.text: It adds nitrogen and protects the soil

quiz.question: Why should you not cultivate deep near the vines?

options.text: Roots near the surface can be cut
Keeps the soil cool and moist and smothers weeds

quiz.question: Why must the hoe be kept away from the vine trunk?

options.text: The trunk will grow too fast
Weeds grow better near the trunk

quiz.question: Who may spray herbicides in the vineyard?

options.text: Only trained, authorised workers with the right PPE
